paragraphs.sourceText: 请于正式开考后半小时内完成该部分，之后将进行听力考试 Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay commenting on the saying “Respect others, and you will be respected.” You can cite examples to illustrate your views. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，评论“尊重他人，你就会受到尊重”这句话。你可以举出例子来阐述你的观点。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre. Questions1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the past 12 months, Nigeria has suffered from a shrinking economy, a sliding currency, and a prolonged fuel shortage. Now, Africa’s largest economy is facing a food crisis as major tomato fields have been destroyed by an insect, leading to a nationwide shortage and escalating prices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 过去12个月，尼日利亚遭受经济萎缩、货币贬值和长期燃料短缺的困扰。现在，非洲最大的经济体正面临粮食危机，主要番茄田被昆虫摧毁，导致全国范围内的短缺和价格上涨。

paragraphs.sourceText: The insect, Tutaabsoluta, has destroyed 80% of farms in Kaduna, Nigeria's largest tomato producing state, leading the government there to declare a state of 26 .The insect, also known as the tomato leaf miner, devastates crops by 27 on fruits and digging into and moving through stalks. It 28 incredibly quickly, breeding up to 12 generations per year if conditions are favorable. It is believed to have 29 in South America in the early 1900s, and later spread to Europe before crossing over to sub-Saharan Africa.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种名为 Tutaabsoluta 的昆虫摧毁了尼日利亚最大的番茄生产州卡杜纳 80% 的农场，导致当地政府宣布进入紧急状态。这种昆虫也称为番茄潜叶蛾，以水果为食，并在茎中挖掘和移动，从而毁坏农作物。它的繁殖速度非常快，如果条件有利的话，每年繁殖多达 12 代。据信它起源于 1900 年代初的南美洲，后来传播到欧洲，最后传播到撒哈拉以南非洲。

paragraphs.sourceText: In Nigeria, where tomatoes are a staple of local diets, the insect's effects are devastating. Retail prices for a 30 of tomatoes at local markets have risen from $0. 50 to $2.50. Farmers are reporting steep losses and a new $20 million tomato-paste factory has 31 production due to the shortages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在尼日利亚，西红柿是当地的主食，这种昆虫的影响是毁灭性的。当地市场上少数西红柿的零售价已从 0 美元上涨。 50 至 2.50 美元。农民报告损失惨重，一家价值 2000 万美元的新番茄酱工厂因短缺而停止生产。

paragraphs.sourceText: Given the moth's ability also to attack crops like pepper and potatoes, Audu Ogbeh, Nigeria's minister of agriculture, has warned that the pest may “create serious problems for food 32 ” in the country. Ogbeh says experts are investigating how to control the pest’s damage and prevent its spread, which has gone largely 33 until now.
paragraphs.translationZh: 鉴于这种飞蛾还能够攻击辣椒和土豆等农作物，尼日利亚农业部长奥杜·奥格贝警告说，这种害虫可能会“给该国的粮食安全带来严重问题”。奥格贝说，专家们正在研究如何控制害虫的损害并防止其蔓延，但到目前为止，这种情况基本上没有得到控制。

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite being the continent's second-largest producer of tomatoes, Nigeria is 34 on $1 billion worth of tomato-paste imports every year. as around 75% of the local harvest goes to waste thanks to a lack of proper storage facilities. A further 35 in local supplies is yet another unwelcome setback to the industry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管尼日利亚是非洲大陆第二大番茄生产国，但每年仍依赖价值 10 亿美元的番茄酱进口。由于缺乏适当的储存设施，当地约 75% 的收成被浪费了。当地供应的进一步减少是该行业的又一个不受欢迎的挫折。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Who’s Really Addicting You to Technology?
paragraphs.translationZh: 谁真正让你对科技上瘾？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) “Nearly everyone I know is addicted in some measure to the Internet,” wrote Tony Schwartz in The New York Times. It’s a common complaint these days. A steady stream of similar headlines accuse the Net and its offspring apps, social media sites and online games of addicting us to distraction
paragraphs.translationZh: A）“几乎我认识的每个人都在某种程度上沉迷于互联网，”托尼·施瓦茨在《纽约时报》上写道。如今，这是一个常见的抱怨。源源不断的类似头条新闻指责网络及其衍生应用程序、社交媒体网站和在线游戏让我们分心。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) There’s little doubt that nearly everyone who comes in contact with the Net has difficulty disconnecting. Many of us, like Schwartz, struggle to stay focused on tasks that require more concentration than it takes to post a status update. As one person ironically put it in the comments section of Schwartz's online article, “As I was reading this very excellent article. I stopped at least half a dozen times to cheek my email.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 毫无疑问，几乎每个接触网络的人都很难脱离网络。我们中的许多人，像施瓦茨一样，很难集中精力完成那些需要比发布状态更新更集中注意力的任务。正如有人在施瓦茨在线文章的评论部分讽刺地指出的那样，“当我阅读这篇非常优秀的文章时。我至少停下来六次检查我的电子邮件。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C) There's something different about this technology: it is both invasive and persuasive. But who's at fault for its overuse？ To find solutions, it's important to understand what we’re dealing with. There are four parties conspiring to keep you connected: the tech, your boss, your friends and you.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 这项技术有一些不同之处：它既具有侵入性又具有说服力。但谁该对它的过度使用负责呢？为了找到解决方案，了解我们正在处理的问题很重要。有四方共同努力让你保持联系：技术人员、你的老板、你的朋友和你自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The technologies themselves, and their makers, are the easiest suspects to blame for our diminishing attention spans. Nicholas Carr, author of The Shallows：What the Internet Is Doing to Our Brains, wrote, “The net is designed to be an interruption system, a machine geared to dividing attention.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 技术本身及其制造者最容易将我们的注意力持续时间的缩短归咎于技术本身。 《浅滩：互联网对我们的大脑做了什么》一书的作者尼古拉斯·卡尔写道：“网络被设计成一个中断系统，一个用来分散注意力的机器。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Online services like Facebook, Twitter and the like, are called out of manipula-tion—making products so good that people can’t stop using them. After studying these products for several years, I wrote a book about how they do it. I learned it all starts with the business model. Since these services rely on advertising revenue, the more frequently you use them, the more money they make. It’s no winder these companies employ teams of people focused on engineering their services to be as engaging as possible. These products aren't habit-forming by chance; it's by design. They have an incentive to keep us hooked.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. Facebook、Twitter 等在线服务被认为是出于操纵——让产品变得如此优秀，以至于人们无法停止使用它们。在研究这些产品几年后，我写了一本关于它们如何做到这一点的书。我了解到这一切都始于商业模式。由于这些服务依赖于广告收入，因此您使用它们的频率越高，它们赚的钱就越多。毫无疑问，这些公司雇佣的团队专注于设计他们的服务，使其尽可能具有吸引力。这些产品的养成并不是偶然的，而是偶然发生的。这是设计使然。他们有动力让我们着迷。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) However, as good as these services are, there are simple steps we can take to keep them at bay. For example, we can change how often we receive the distracting notifications that trigger our urge to check. According to Adam Marchick, CEO of mobile marketing company Kahuna, less than 15 percent of smartphone users ever bother to adjust their notification settlings--meaning the remaining 85 percent of us default to the app makers' every preset trigger. Google and Apple have made it far too difficult to adjust these settings so it's up to us to take steps ensure we set these triggers to suit our own needs, not the needs of the app makers’.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 然而，尽管这些服务很好，但我们可以采取一些简单的步骤来阻止它们。例如，我们可以改变接收分散注意力的通知的频率，这些通知会引发我们检查的冲动。移动营销公司 Kahuna 的首席执行官 Adam Marchick 表示，只有不到 15% 的智能手机用户曾经费心去调整他们的通知设置，这意味着剩下的 85% 的人默认应用程序制造商的每个预设触发器。谷歌和苹果让调整这些设置变得非常困难，因此我们有责任采取措施，确保我们设置这些触发器以满足我们自己的需求，而不是应用程序制造商的需求。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) While companies like Facebook harvest attention to generate revenue from advertisers, other technologies have no such agenda. Take email, for example. This system couldn’t care less how often you use it. Yet to many, email is the most habit-forming medium of all. We check email at all hours of the day—we’re obsessed, But why? Because that’s what the boss wants. For almost all white-collar jobs, email is the primary tool of corporate communication, A slow response to a message could hurt not only your reputation but also your livelihood.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 虽然像 Facebook 这样的公司通过吸引注意力来从广告商那里获得收入，但其他技术却没有这样的议程。以电子邮件为例。这个系统不在乎你使用它的频率。然而对许多人来说，电子邮件是最容易养成习惯的媒介。我们全天随时查看电子邮件——我们着迷，但为什么呢？因为这就是老板想要的。对于几乎所有白领工作来说，电子邮件是企业沟通的主要工具，对消息的缓慢响应不仅会损害您的声誉，还会损害您的生计。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. Your friends are also responsible. Think about this familiar scene. People gathered around a table, enjoying food and each other’s company. There’s laughter and a bit of kidding. Then, during an interval in the conversation, someone takes out their phone to check who knows what. Barely anyone notices and no one says a thing.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 你的朋友也有责任。想想这个熟悉的场景。人们围坐在桌子旁，享受美食和彼此的陪伴。有笑声和一点开玩笑。然后，在谈话间隙，有人拿出手机查看谁知道什么。几乎没有人注意到，也没有人说什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Now imagine the same dinner, but instead of checking their phone, the person belches(打嗝）-loudly. Everyone notices. Unless the meal takes place in a beer house, this is considered bad manners. The impolite act violates the basic rules of etiquette. One has to wonder: why don’t we apply the same social norms to checking phones during meals, meetings and conversations as we do to other antisocial behaviors? Somehow, we accept it and say nothing when someone offends.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我）现在想象一下同样的晚餐，但这个人没有检查手机，而是打嗝——大声。每个人都注意到了。除非在啤酒屋里用餐，否则这被认为是不礼貌的行为。这种不礼貌的行为违反了基本的礼仪规则。人们不得不想：为什么我们不像对待其他反社会行为一样，在吃饭、开会和谈话时检查手机时采用同样的社会规范？不知何故，当有人冒犯时，我们接受了并且什么也不说。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The reality is taking one’s phone out at the wrong time is worse than belching because, unlike other minor offense, checking tech is contagious. Once one person looks at their phone, other people feel compelled to do the same, starting a chain reaction. The more people are on their phones, the fewer people are talking until finally you are the only one left not reading email or checking Twitter. From a societal perspective, phone checking is less like belching in public and more like another bad habit. Our phones are like cigarettes-something to do when we’re anxious, bored or when our fingers need something to toy with Seeing others enjoy a smoke, or sneak a quick glance, is too tempting to resist and soon everyone is doing it.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 现实情况是，在错误的时间拿出手机比打嗝更糟糕，因为与其他轻微的冒犯不同，检查电子产品具有传染性。一旦一个人看了一下自己的手机，其他人就会觉得有必要这样做，从而引发连锁反应。使用手机的人越多，说话的人就越少，直到最后你成为唯一一个不阅读电子邮件或查看 Twitter 的人。从社会角度来看，打电话检查不像在公共场合打嗝，而更像是另一种坏习惯。我们的手机就像香烟——当我们焦虑、无聊或者手指需要玩玩的时候，我们可以使用手机。看到别人抽烟，或者瞥一眼，太诱人了，无法抗拒，很快每个人都开始这么做了。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The technology, your boss, and your friends, all influence how often you find yourself using (or overusing )these gadgets. But there’s still someone who deserves scrutiny--the person holding the phone.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 技术、你的老板和你的朋友都会影响你发现自己使用（或过度使用）这些小工具的频率。但还有一个人值得仔细审视——那个拿着电话的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) I have a confession. Even though I study habit-forming technology for a living, disconnecting is not easy for me. I'm online far more than I'd like. Like Schwartz and so many others, I often find myself distracted and off tack. I wanted to know why so I began self-monitoring to try to understand my behavior. That's when I discovered an uncomfortable truth. I use technology as an escape. When I'm doing something I'd rather not do, or when I'm someplace I'd rather not be, I use my phone to port myself elsewhere. I found that this ability to instantly shift my attention was often a good thing, like when passing time on public transportation, But frequently my tech use was not so benign. When I faced difficult work, like thinking through an article idea or editing the same draft for the hundredth time, for example, a more sinister screen would draw me in. I could easily escape discomfort. temporarily. by answering email or browsing the web under the pretense of so-called “research.” Though I desperately wanted to lay blame elsewhere, I finally had to admit that my bad habits had less to do with new-age. technology and more to do with old-fashioned procrastination(拖延）
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 我有一个坦白。尽管我以研究养成习惯的技术为生，但脱离对我来说并不容易。我上网的次数远远超出了我的预期。像施瓦茨和其他许多人一样，我经常发现自己心烦意乱、偏离轨道。我想知道为什么，所以我开始自我监控，试图了解自己的行为。就在那时我发现了一个令人不安的事实。我用科技作为逃避的方式。当我正在做一些我不想做的事情，或者当我在某个我不想去的地方时，我会用手机将自己转移到其他地方。我发现这种立即转移注意力的能力通常是一件好事，就像在公共交通上消磨时间一样，但我对科技的使用常常不是那么良性。当我面临困难的工作时，例如思考一篇文章的想法或编辑同一个草稿一百次，例如，一个更险恶的屏幕会吸引我。我可以很容易地逃避不适。暂时地。以所谓的“研究”为幌子回复电子邮件或浏览网页。尽管我非常想把责任归咎于其他地方，但我最终不得不承认我的坏习惯与新时代关系不大。技术以及更多与老式拖延症有关的东西（条纹）

paragraphs.sourceText: M) It's easy to blame technology for being so distracting, but distraction is nothing new. Aristotle and Socrates debated the nature of “akrasia”--our tendency to do things against our interests. If we're honest with ourselves, tech is just another way to occupy our time and minds, If we weren’t on our devices. We’d likely do similarly unproductive.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 人们很容易将注意力分散归咎于技术，但分散注意力并不是什么新鲜事。亚里士多德和苏格拉底讨论了“akrasia”的本质——我们倾向于做违背自己利益的事情。如果我们对自己诚实的话，如果我们不在我们的设备上，科技只是占用我们时间和思想的另一种方式。我们很可能也会做同样的低效事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Personal technology is indeed more engaging than ever, and there's no doubt companies are engineering their products and services to be more compelling and attractive. But would we want it any other way? The intended result of making something better is that people use it more. That's not necessarily a problem, that's progress.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 个人技术确实比以往任何时候都更具吸引力，毫无疑问，公司正在设计他们的产品和服务，使其更具吸引力和吸引力。但我们想要其他方式吗？使某物变得更好的预期结果是人们更多地使用它。这不一定是问题，这就是进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. These improvements don't mean we shouldn't attempt to control our use of technology. In order to make sure it doesn't control us, we should come to terms with the fact that it's more than the technology itself that’s responsible for our habits. Our workplace culture, social norms and individual behaviors all play a part. To put technology in its place, we must be conscious not only of how technology is changing, but also of how it is changing us.
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 这些改进并不意味着我们不应该尝试控制技术的使用。为了确保它不会控制我们，我们应该接受这样一个事实：影响我们习惯的不仅仅是技术本身。我们的工作场所文化、社会规范和个人行为都发挥着一定作用。为了让技术发挥其应有的作用，我们不仅必须意识到技术正在如何改变，而且还必须意识到它正在如何改变我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36.Online services are so designed that the more they are used, the more profit they generate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36.在线服务的设计宗旨是使用越多，产生的利润就越多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The author admits using technology as an escape from the task at hand.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: You may have heard that Coca-Cola once contained an ingredient capable of sparking particular devotion in consumers: cocaine. The cocaine. The “coca” in the name referred to the extracts of coca leaf that the drink's originator, chemist John Pemberton, mixed with his sugary syrup( 浆汁). At the time, coca leaf extract mixed with wine was a common tonic( 滋补品), and Pemberton's sweet brew was a way to get around local laws prohibiting the sale of alcohol. But the other half of the name represents another ingredient, less infamous(名声不好的), perhaps, but also strangely potent: the kola nut.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可能听说过，可口可乐曾经含有一种能够激发消费者特别喜爱的成分：可卡因。可卡因。名称中的“古柯”指的是古柯叶提取物，该饮料的创始人化学家约翰·彭伯顿将其与他的糖浆（浆汁）混合。当时，古柯叶提取物与葡萄酒混合是一种常见的滋补品，而彭伯顿的甜酒是规避当地禁止销售酒精的法律的一种方式。但这个名字的另一半代表着另一种成分，也许不那么臭名昭著，但也有奇怪的功效：可乐果。

paragraphs.sourceText: In West Africa, people have long chewed kola nuts as stimulants, because they contain caffeine that also occurs naturally in tea, coffee ,and chocolate .They also have heart stimulants .
paragraphs.translationZh: 在西非，人们长期咀嚼可乐果作为兴奋剂，因为它们含有天然存在于茶、咖啡和巧克力中的咖啡因。它们还具有心脏兴奋剂的作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Historian Paul Lovejoy relates that the cultivation of kola nuts in West Africa is hundreds of years old. The leafy, spreading trees were planted on graves and as part of traditional rituals. Even though the nuts, which need to stay moist, can be somewhat delicate to transport, traders carried them hundreds of miles throughout the forests and grasslands.
paragraphs.translationZh: 历史学家保罗·洛夫乔伊 (Paul Lovejoy) 表示，西非可乐果的种植已有数百年历史。这些绿叶茂盛、蔓延的树木被种植在坟墓上，也是传统仪式的一部分。尽管这些坚果需要保持湿润，运输起来可能有些困难，但商人还是将它们运送到数百英里的森林和草原上。

paragraphs.sourceText: Europeans did not know of them until the 1500s when Portuguese ships arrived on the coast of what is now Sierra Leone. And while the Portuguese took part in the trade, ferrying nuts down the coast along with other goods, by 1620, when English explorer Richard Jobson made his way up the Gambia, the nuts were still peculiar to his eyes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 直到 1500 年代，当葡萄牙船只抵达现在的塞拉利昂海岸时，欧洲人才知道它们。虽然葡萄牙人参与了贸易，将坚果与其他货物一起沿海岸运输，但到了 1620 年，当英国探险家理查德·乔布森 (Richard Jobson) 沿着冈比亚航行时，坚果在他眼中仍然很奇特。

paragraphs.sourceText: By the late 19th century, kola nuts were being shipped by the tonne to Europe and the US. Many made their way into medicines, intended as a kind of energy boost. One such popular medicinal drink was Vin Mariani, a French product consisting of coca extract mixed with red wine. It was created by a French chemist, Angelo Mariani, in 1863. So when Pemberton created his drink, it represented an ongoing trend. When cocaine eventually fell from grace as a beverage ingredient, kola-extract colas became popular.
paragraphs.translationZh: 到 19 世纪末，可乐果已成吨运往欧洲和美国。许多药物被制成药物，目的是作为一种能量增强剂。 Vin Mariani 是一种流行的药用饮料，它是一种法国产品，由古柯提取物与红酒混合而成。它是由法国化学家 Angelo Mariani 于 1863 年发明的。因此，当 Pemberton 发明他的饮料时，它代表了一种持续的趋势。当可卡因最终不再作为饮料成分时，可乐提取物可乐开始流行。

paragraphs.sourceText: The first year it was available, Coca-Cola averaged nine servings a day across all the Atlanta soda fountains where it was sold. As it grew more popular, the company sold rights to bottle the soda, so it could travel easily. Today about 1. 9 billion Cokes are purchased daily. It's become so iconic that attempts to change its taste in 1985- sweetening it in a move projected to boost sales proved disastrous, with widespread anger from consumers. "Coca-Cola Classic" returned to store shelves just three months after the "New Coke" was released.
paragraphs.translationZh: 上市第一年，可口可乐在所有销售该产品的亚特兰大冷饮店平均每天提供九份。随着它越来越受欢迎，该公司出售了这种苏打水的装瓶权，这样它就可以方便地运输。如今，每天大约购买 1. 9 亿可乐。它已变得如此具有标志性，以至于 1985 年试图改变其口味，旨在提高销量，但结果却是灾难性的，引起了消费者的广泛愤怒。 “新可乐”发布三个月后，“经典可口可乐”又重新回到商店货架上。

paragraphs.sourceText: These days, the Coca-Cola recipe is a closely guarded secret. But it's said to no longer contain kola nut extract, relying instead on artificial imitations to achieve the flavour.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如今，可口可乐的配方已成为严格保守的秘密。但据说它不再含有可乐果提取物，而是依靠人工仿制品来实现风味。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 51 至 55 题基于以下段落

paragraphs.sourceText: Twenty years ago, the Urban Land Institute defined the two types of cities that dominated the US landscape: smaller cities that operated around standard 9-5 business hours and large metropolitan areas that ran all 24 hours of the day. Analyzing and comparing cities using the lens of this basic divide gives interesting context to how investment capital flows and housing prices have shifted.
paragraphs.translationZh: 二十年前，城市土地研究所定义了主导美国景观的两种类型的城市：标准工作时间朝九晚五的小城市和全天 24 小时运行的大都市区。使用这一基本鸿沟的视角来分析和比较城市，为投资资本流动和房价的变化提供了有趣的背景。

paragraphs.sourceText: In recent years, many mid-sized cities have begun to adopt a middle-of-the-road approach incorporating the excitement and opportunity of large cities with small cities’ quiet after midnight.These18-hour cities are beginning to make waves in real estate rankings and attract more real estate investment. What is underlying this new movement in real estate, and why do these cities have so much appeal?
paragraphs.translationZh: 近年来，许多中等城市开始采取中间路线，将大城市的热闹和机遇与小城市午夜后的安静融为一体。这些18小时城市开始在房地产排名中掀起波澜，吸引更多的房地产投资。这一新的房地产运动的背后是什么？为什么这些城市具有如此大的吸引力？

paragraphs.sourceText: 18-hour cities combine the best of 24-hour and 9-5 cities, which contributes to downtown revitalization. For decades, many downtown cores in small to mid-sized cities were abandoned after work hours by workers who lived in the suburbs. Movement out of city centers was widespread, and downtown tenants were predominantly made up of the working poor. This generated little commerce for downtown businesses in the evenings, which made business and generating tax revenue for municipal upkeep difficult. With the rise of a new concept in urban planning that aims to make life easier and more convenient, increasing popularity for urban areas that caused the real estate pushes, in major cities like San Francisco or New York, has inspired a type of forward thinking urbanity and in smaller cities
paragraphs.translationZh: 18小时城市结合了24小时和9-5城市的优点，有助于市中心的复兴。几十年来，许多中小城市的市中心核心区在下班后被居住在郊区的工人抛弃。迁出市中心的现象十分普遍，市中心的租户主要由贫困工人组成。这使得市中心的企业在晚上几乎没有商业活动，这使得商业和为市政维护创造税收变得困难。随着旨在让生活更轻松、更方便的城市规划新概念的兴起，城市地区的日益普及导致了房地产的推动，在旧金山或纽约等大城市，激发了一种前瞻性的城市化，而在较小的城市

paragraphs.sourceText: Transforming downtown areas so that they incorporate modern housing and improved walkability to local restaurants, retail, and entertainment -especially when combined with improved infrastructure for cyclists and public transit-makes them appeal to a more affluent demographic. These adjustments encourage employers in the knowledge and talent industries to keep their offices downtown. Access to foot traffic and proximity to transit allow the type of entertainment-oriented businesses such as bars and restaurants to stay open later, which attracts both younger, creative workers and baby boomers nearing retirement alike. Because of their smaller size, most keep hours that allow people to enjoy themselves, then have some quiet after midnight, as opposed to large major cities like New York, where the buzz of activity is ongoing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对市中心地区进行改造，使其融入现代化的住房，并改善当地餐馆、零售和娱乐场所的步行性，特别是与改善骑自行车者和公共交通的基础设施相结合，使它们吸引更富裕的人群。这些调整鼓励知识和人才行业的雇主将办公室保留在市中心。人流量大、交通便利，酒吧和餐馆等以娱乐为导向的企业可以延长营业时间，这吸引了年轻的创意工作者和即将退休的婴儿潮一代。由于规模较小，大多数城市都会安排让人们尽情享受的时间，然后在午夜后享受一些安静，这与纽约等大城市不同，那里的活动不断热闹。

paragraphs.sourceText: These 18-hour cities are rapidly on the rise and offer great opportunities for homeowner investment. In many of these cities such as Denver, a diverse and vigorous economy attracted to the urban core has offered stable employment for residents. The right urban mix has propped up home occupancy, increased property values, and attracted significant investment capital.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些18小时城市正在迅速崛起，为业主投资提供了绝佳机会。在丹佛等许多城市中，多元化而充满活力的经济吸引了城市核心，为居民提供了稳定的就业机会。正确的城市组合提振了住房入住率，提高了房地产价值，并吸引了大量投资资本。
